_about: Does a search run in the language the person was speaking?
Every `said` here is a real Korean turn from runtime/koreanSession.log
or runtime/koreanSession2.log, or a turn of the same shape; every
`router_query` is what the router produced for it, or its shape.
expect  rewritten = the search runs on the person's own words
kept      = the router's wording stands, and why
The kept half is not padding. A turn that leans on the one before it
does not carry its own subject, and searching those words alone is
worse than the English query rather than better -- the subject the
conversation is holding is stored in English, so there is nothing in
Korean to put back. Korean leans back in two ways a first version of
this rule missed: from the middle of the sentence ('그 섬에 카지노가
있는지'), and by simply leaving the subject out ('얼마나 많은 사람들이
봤는데'). A matrix without those would score 100% on a rule that
